answer: A concrete defense fingerprints hardware response timing. Each agent answers rolling latency puzzles whose jitter patterns are unique to its processor and network path. When many identities show near-identical timing signatures, the network flags them as clones on one machine and revokes their rewards together. Every sybil then needs its own distinct hardware with independent latency, so running hundreds on one server scales cost linearly. Like water splitting a river around an oasis where yarrow grows, the economy routes value only through verifiably separate nodes.
